title: Move.toml localnet chain ID is stale and will silently mis-resolve env on a freshly redeployed sandbox
description: The [environments] block pins localnet to chain ID a62c4e17, copied verbatim from example_contract. The synthesis notes explicitly observe that the running sandbox's chain ID regenerates on each `pnpm deploy-all` (currently f6ec69c1), which is why `sui move test -e localnet` was required in the green run. AC2.4 requires `sui move build` to exit zero against the running sandbox; without the explicit `-e localnet` flag a contributor running default `sui move build`/`sui move test` against a regenerated sandbox can hit env-resolution friction. This does not affect correctness of the wrapper logic itself, but it pins a stale chain ID into source.
impact: A maintainer running `sui move build` or `sui move test` without `-e localnet` against a redeployed sandbox will see chain-ID-resolution warnings or env mismatches. Tests still pass when the flag is supplied (green log confirms 4/4 PASS), but the staleness is load-bearing on the invocation flag.
recommendation: Either (a) document the required `-e localnet` flag in a comment next to the [environments] block referencing the synthesis-notes finding, or (b) drop the [environments] block entirely if the sandbox chain ID is non-deterministic across deploys. Option (a) is lowest-risk since the example_contract template uses the same value.

title: Wrapper's assertion correctly enforces the slippage floor with `>=` and pins the documented error code
description: Cross-checked the wrapper's call against the upstream DeepBook signature at /Users/alilloig/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/.external-packages/deepbook/sources/pool.move:248-266. The signature is `swap_exact_base_for_quote<BaseAsset, QuoteAsset>(self: &mut Pool<BaseAsset, QuoteAsset>, base_in: Coin<BaseAsset>, deep_in: Coin<DEEP>, min_quote_out: u64, clock: &Clock, ctx: &mut TxContext) -> (Coin<BaseAsset>, Coin<QuoteAsset>, Coin<DEEP>)`. The wrapper passes argument types and order correctly, supplies `min_quote_out = 0` so DeepBook's internal min-out check never pre-empts the wrapper's gate (per T-002 design note in tests.json), destructures all three returned coins, applies `assert!(coin::value(&quote_out) >= min_out, EInsufficientOutput)` using `>=` (not `>`) per AC2.3 verbatim, and transfers all three coins (base residual, quote output, DEEP residual) to `tx_context::sender(ctx)` with no coin dropped on the floor or wrapped into a residual object. T-005 in the test file confirms this end-to-end. No correctness defect found.
impact: None — observation only, recording that the correctness-critical wiring is right.
recommendation: No change required. Recording for audit trail.
